mil3.1.1:1.1: Then King Milinda went to Venerable Nāgasena and exchanged greetings with him. After exchanging courteous, memorable conversation, he sat down to one side.
mil3.1.1:1.2: And Venerable Nāgasena, with a courteous greeting in return, also pleased the mind of King Milinda.
mil3.1.1:2.1: Then King Milinda said to Venerable Nāgasena—
mil3.1.1:2.2: “How is your reverence known? What is your name, venerable sir?”
mil3.1.1:2.3: “I am known, Great King, as ‘Nāgasena’; my fellow practitioners of the spiritual life address me as ‘Nāgasena’. And my parents give a name too—‘Nāgasena’, or ‘Sūrasena’, or ‘Vīrasena’, or ‘Sīhasena’. But still, Great King, what is called Nāgasena is just a reckoning, an appellation, a designation, a usage, a mere name; for no person is found here.”
mil3.1.1:3.2: “Listen to me, sirs, five hundred Yonakas and eighty thousand mendicants: this Nāgasena has said—
mil3.1.1:3.3: ‘No person is found here.’ Is it proper to approve of that?”
mil3.1.1:3.4: Then King Milinda said to Venerable Nāgasena—
mil3.1.1:3.5: “If, Venerable Nāgasena, no person is found, then who gives you the requisites of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick? Who uses them? Who guards ethics? Who practices meditation? Who realizes the paths, the fruits, and extinguishment? Who kills living beings? Who takes what is not given? Who commits sexual misconduct? Who speaks falsely? Who drinks liquor? Who commits one of the five deeds with immediate result? Therefore there is no skillful, there is no unskillful; there is no doer or instigator of skillful and unskillful deeds; there is no fruit or result of deeds well done and badly done. If, Venerable Nāgasena, someone were to kill you, for him too there would be no killing of a living being; and you too, Venerable Nāgasena, have no teacher, no preceptor, no full ordination.
mil3.1.1:3.6: You say, ‘My fellow practitioners of the spiritual life address me as Nāgasena, Great King’; but who here is Nāgasena?
mil3.1.1:3.52: “Well then, venerable sir, are form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness taken together Nāgasena?”
mil3.1.1:3.54: “Well then, venerable sir, is Nāgasena something apart from form, feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness?”
mil3.1.1:3.56: “Though I ask and ask about him, venerable sir, I do not see Nāgasena.
mil3.1.1:3.57: Is it only the name Nāgasena, venerable sir, that is Nāgasena?”
mil3.1.1:3.59: “Then who here is Nāgasena? You are speaking falsehood, venerable sir, a lie; there is no Nāgasena.”
mil3.1.1:4.1: Then Venerable Nāgasena said to King Milinda—
mil3.1.1:4.2: “You, Great King, are a delicate aristocrat, exceedingly delicate. When you come on foot at midday, Great King, trampling on the scorching ground, on hot sand, on rough gravel and potsherds, your feet hurt, your body tires, your mind is afflicted, and body-consciousness accompanied by suffering arises. Did you come on foot, or by conveyance?”
mil3.1.1:4.3: “I did not come on foot, venerable sir; I came in a chariot.”
mil3.1.1:4.4: “If you came in a chariot, Great King, tell me about the chariot. Is the pole the chariot, Great King?”
mil3.1.1:4.20: “Well then, Great King, are the pole, axle, wheels, frame, staff, yoke, reins, and goad taken together the chariot?”
mil3.1.1:4.22: “Well then, Great King, is the chariot something apart from the pole, axle, wheels, frame, staff, yoke, reins, and goad?”
mil3.1.1:4.24: “Though I ask and ask about it, Great King, I do not see a chariot.
mil3.1.1:4.25: Is it only the word for chariot, Great King, that is the chariot?”
mil3.1.1:4.27: “Then what here is the chariot? You are speaking falsehood, Great King, a lie; there is no chariot. You, Great King, are the foremost king in all Jambudīpa; out of fear of whom do you speak a lie? Listen to me, sirs, five hundred Yonakas and eighty thousand mendicants: this King Milinda has said—
mil3.1.1:4.28: ‘I came in a chariot’; but if you, Great King, came in a chariot, and when told ‘Tell me about the chariot’ you cannot produce a chariot, is it proper to approve of that?”
mil3.1.1:5.1: When this was said, the five hundred Yonakas applauded Venerable Nāgasena and said to King Milinda—
mil3.1.1:5.2: “Now, Great King, speak, if you are able.”
mil3.1.1:6.1: Then King Milinda said to Venerable Nāgasena—
mil3.1.1:6.2: “I am not speaking falsely, Venerable Nāgasena. Depending on the pole, depending on the axle, depending on the wheels, depending on the frame, and depending on the staff, ‘chariot’ comes about as a reckoning, an appellation, a designation, a usage, a mere name.”
mil3.1.1:7.1: “Well done, Great King, you understand the chariot;
mil3.1.1:7.2: so too, Great King, depending on my hair and depending on my body hair … and depending on the brain in the skull, and depending on form, depending on feeling, depending on perception, depending on formations, and depending on consciousness, ‘Nāgasena’ comes about as a reckoning, an appellation, a designation, a usage, a mere name; but in the ultimate sense, no person is found here.
mil3.1.1:7.3: This too, Great King, was said by the nun Vajirā in the presence of the Blessed One—
mil3.1.1:9.1: “How wonderful, Venerable Nāgasena, how marvelous, Venerable Nāgasena, that such exceedingly ingenious questions have been answered! If the Buddha were still living he would applaud: well done, well done, Nāgasena, such exceedingly ingenious questions have been answered!”
